severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — PROFESSIONAL NARRATIVE INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: FABRICATED-PARABLE FRONT STALLS OVER THE LINKEDIN PLATEAU AS AI-GENERATED WORKPLACE FABLES FLOOD FEEDS WITH HEROIC INTERVIEWS THAT NEVER HAPPENED, JANITORS WHO DELIVERED FORTUNE-500 WISDOM, AND SINGLE-SENTENCE PARAGRAPHS DESCENDING LIKE HAIL
advisory: The National Slop Service has upgraded conditions across the LinkedIn Plateau to a SEVERE SLOP WARNING effective immediately. A deep low-pressure system of synthetic inspiration is generating sustained engagement-bait: fictional anecdotes in which the poster boldly rejects a candidate, then learns a humbling lesson, then closes with a question for the comment section. Residents are advised that no such meeting occurred, no such candidate existed, and the 'everyone clapped' was, meteorologically speaking, zero clapping. Line breaks are falling faster than they can be absorbed.

regional_outlook.conditions: Severe fabricated-parable activity with gusting humility. Expect dense accumulations of single-sentence paragraphs and a 60 percent chance of 'Agree?' by late afternoon.
Spillover flooding as the same fable arrives repackaged as a 'thought leadership' newsletter. Unsubscribe links functioning normally but emotionally unreachable.
The parable reappears screenshot-stripped of attribution and presented as breaking fact. Visibility near zero; context not expected to return this week.
Warm moist nostalgia feeds the system as the fable mutates into a 'my grandfather ran a hardware store' format. High engagement, low grandfather.
Scattered aggregation showers as content farms index all forty versions of the story, each cited as the original source of the other thirty-nine.

specimen.status: Overabundant; peak breeding season year-round, no natural predators except the scroll
specimen.habitat: Nests on the LinkedIn Plateau; migrates to the Inbox Estuary when feeds become saturated
specimen.field_marks: Opens with a confident declarative hook ('I fired my top salesperson today.'). Body descends in single-sentence paragraphs, each isolated like a startled bird. Reliably features a janitor, an intern, or a quiet candidate who delivers wisdom no employee has ever delivered. Terminates in a one-word question and a call to repost.
specimen.call: I almost didn't hire her. Then she said something that changed everything. Thoughts?
specimen.confusion_species: Can be mistaken for a genuine professional reflection from a real person who actually learned something. Distinguish by the absence of specifics: real stories name the product, the quarter, and the awkward silence; the Fable names only The Lesson, and the lesson is always that the poster was right to be vulnerable in public.

spotter_tip: Count the line breaks. If a four-sentence anecdote occupies the vertical space of a lease agreement, you are observing the Boardroom Fable in full display plumage. A real story has margins; slop has only drama and whitespace.
tomorrow: Fabricated-parable front weakens slightly as the system cycles into 'unpopular opinion:' formation; residual humility lingering through the evening commute.
